name: The Dragon Tree of Campo da Barca

location.address: Jardim do Campo da Barca, Estrada Conde Carvalhal, Funchal

official_register.name: ASMAC 081 (Arvores e Arboledas Singulares da Macaronesia, VALCONMAC); also Funchal PDM Quadro 5 code 256 (Jardins do Campo da Barca, Dragoeiro)

access: Free. Small municipal garden in central Funchal, open public space (Funchal City Council park; reopened after 2012 works, further works on the north sector planned 2024-25).
transport: Central Funchal, about 1 km (roughly 15 minutes on foot) east of the Municipal Garden; about 500 m from Jardim Almirante Reis (by coordinates).
story:
A register of the singular trees of Macaronesia chose this one for its size, and gives its height as five and a half metres. The register does not reconcile the two, and neither will we. It measured the trunk at 2.52 metres round at the base and called it a magnificent specimen standing on its own. It is the only dragon tree in the Jardim do Campo da Barca, and Funchal's municipal plan lists it too, under code 256.

The garden is small. Its south part dates from 1818 and the city has run it since 1897. Three thousand square metres, cut in two by the Estrada Conde Carvalhal, with the Largo Conde Canavial to the north and the Praça de Tenerife to the south. Portuguese Wikipedia calls the dragon tree the most emblematic tree in it.

It has outlasted at least one neighbour. In November 2021 a tree came down in this garden, and the press named it as a Mediterranean hackberry. The dragon tree is still there, logged by visitors on iNaturalist as recently as December 2025.

Our pin marks the garden, not the crown, because no source places the trunk exactly. With one dragon tree in a garden this size that costs you a minute, and in June 2026 the council put up new bilingual signs naming the monumental trees here. And nobody has dated it. The 1818 garden says nothing about when this tree went in. If you know, tell us.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise it as the only dragon tree in the Jardim do Campo da Barca, 5.5 metres tall and 2.52 metres round at the base, standing on its own. It is in the small garden either side of the Estrada Conde Carvalhal.
verify_notes: Register facts: ASMAC 081 'Drago de Jardin de Campo da Barca': Dracaena draco, reason for selection 'size', not a grove, height 5.5 m, maximum perimeter 2.52 m (at the base), age 'no reference'; description: 'magnificent specimen standing isolated in the Campo da Barca garden'. Also listed as code 256 'Dragoeiro' under Jardins do Campo da Barca in Funchal PDM Quadro 5 (Relatorio de Fundamentacao Vol II, March 2018); the PDM table was read from the PDF, same tree numbering as the island register. pt.wikipedia: garden is 3,000 m2, split by Estrada Conde Carvalhal into north sector (Largo Conde Canavial, ~1,000 m2) and south sector (Praca de Tenerife, ~2,000 m2); garden dates from 1818 (south part), municipal since 1897; the dragon tree is 'the most emblematic tree of this garden'. A Visit Madeira style guide text (surfaced by search, not fetched) puts it at the south end with a large rounded crown. Funchal City Council news of 2026-06-03 (fetched): new bilingual signs at Parque de Santa Catarina, Jardim Municipal and Jardins do Campo da Barca identify the municipal monumental trees in each. ALIVE: iNaturalist observations of Dracaena draco inside the garden 2021 to 2025-12-16 (e.g. 330956411, 5 m accuracy); Commons file 'Drachenbaum Funchal.jpg' (CC BY-SA 4.0, Hans-Jurgen Hubner, 2023-07-23) is captioned 'the only dragon tree in Jardim do Campo da Barca', which settles identity. Photo in reach: that Commons file (not downloaded). PIN: garden level only. iNaturalist fixes of dragon trees cluster at about 32.6503,-16.9030 (5 observations 2021-2025) and a second pair near 32.6498,-16.9018; Wikipedia puts the garden's south sector (Praca de Tenerife) at about 32.6493,-16.9027, so the exact crown could not be placed from sources; coordinate given is the middle of those. Do not claim confirmed. Age: none in any source; the girth of 2.52 m and 5.5 m height are modest for a dragon tree, so no age should be derived. A different tree fell in the garden on 2021-11-05 (a Celtis australis, jornaleconomico.sapo.pt), not the dragon tree. Sanity: dragon trees grow slowly, 5.5 m is plausible. Single register + wikipedia + photo caption; flagged. Nominatim shows the garden as OSM way 293439462 (north sector, 32.6512,-16.9020).
